name: Slovenian Potica
description: Potica, Slovenia's cherished walnut roll, is a genuine symbol of family tradition, made for Christmas, Easter, and weddings for generations - real technique stretches the yeasted dough paper-thin, rolls it tightly while stretching slightly with each turn, and pokes it all over with a skewer both before and after the egg wash, which is what lets steam escape properly during baking rather than tearing the layers apart.
steps_detailed: Warm the milk and melted butter together until just warm, then mix with the flour and egg yolk into a soft, elastic dough. Let rise 60-90 minutes until doubled.
Warm the honey and cream together, then mix into the ground walnuts with the cinnamon until spreadable.
Roll the dough out paper-thin on a floured surface.
Spread the walnut filling evenly over the dough, then roll up tightly from one end, stretching the dough gently as you go to keep the layers thin.
Place in a buttered loaf pan and poke all over with a skewer.
Let rise 30-40 minutes more, then brush with a little beaten egg and poke the holes again, all the way to the bottom.
Bake at 350F (175C) for 35-40 minutes until deeply golden.

name: Slovenian Jota (Bean and Sauerkraut Stew)
description: Jota, a real hearty bean and sauerkraut stew with smoked meat, is a genuine Slovenian winter staple, real technique simmering long enough for the sauerkraut's sharpness to mellow and meld with the beans.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Cowpeas (blackeyes), immature seeds, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

steps_detailed: Cook the bacon and garlic together, 3-4 minutes.
Add the beans, sauerkraut, potato, and 2 cups water, and simmer 30-35 minutes until the flavors meld and the sauerkraut mellows.

name: Slovenian Štruklji
description: Štruklji, rolled dumplings filled with real cottage cheese, are a genuine Slovenian staple, real technique rolls the filled dough into a log, wraps it in cloth, and steams it before slicing.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour and egg with a little water into a soft dough. Rest 15 minutes.
Mix the cottage cheese with the sour cream for the filling.
Roll the dough thin, spread the filling evenly, and roll up into a log.
Wrap tightly in cloth and steam over simmering water 25-30 minutes.
Slice and drizzle with the melted butter before serving.

name: Slovenian Cucumber Salad
description: A simple vinegar-dressed cucumber salad, a common Slovenian side, real technique salting the cucumber first to draw out excess water.
steps_detailed: Salt the cucumber slices and let sit 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Whisk the vinegar, oil, and sugar together, and toss with the cucumber.

name: Slovenian Roasted Walnuts
description: A simple roasted walnut snack, walnuts being central to Slovenian baking tradition.
steps_detailed: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant.

name: Slovenian Beef and Vegetable Stew

Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.
